games.info: NLDS Game 3, series 1-1 | 6:00 PM ET, Truist Park, FS1

away_sp.name: Yoshinobu Yamamoto
away_sp.notes: 14-9; books price 18+ outs at -163, so ~6 innings

home_sp.name: Chris Sale
home_sp.notes: 14-9, 6.0 IP per start; HR allowed not found, so FIP uses league HR rate

why: Sale held the Dodgers to 2 earned runs in 16 innings this year, including an 11-strikeout shutout on Aug 27.
The Dodgers went right-handed against him: Ohtani dropped to 5th (cold since coming off the IL); Kiké and Rojas start over Muncy and Edman.
Yamamoto has a 0.55 ERA in three career starts against Atlanta, so expect a tight game.
Both bullpens had Monday off. Atlanta's Fuentes and Iglesias closed out Game 2.
moves: Total opened 6.5 (under −118) and dropped to 6 after almost all early money hit the under.
By first pitch the moneyline was a pick'em (LAD −110 / ATL −109); one report has Atlanta opening −115.

games.info: NLDS Game 3, MIL leads 2-0 | 9:30 PM ET, Petco Park, FS1

away_sp.name: Dustin May
away_sp.notes: ip/gs estimated; books' outs line 8.5 (about 3 innings); 5.65 ERA since joining MIL

home_sp.name: Nick Pivetta
home_sp.notes: ip estimated; missed Apr 12 - Sep 8 (flexor strain), 3.1 IP in Wild Card start

why: Milwaukee is the better team (+214 run differential against about +41), and May had a 1.23 ERA in three starts against San Diego this year.

Books expect a short May start (outs line 8.5, about 3 innings); he hasn't gotten past the 3rd inning in his last 3 starts. That hands the game to a Brewers bullpen whose top three arms each pitched Games 1 and 2, while San Diego's is fully rested.
Pivetta has a 1.45 ERA in four starts since a five-month elbow injury, but went only 3.1 innings in his Wild Card start.
Hot night: about 82°F at first pitch under an extreme-heat warning, which helps the ball carry. Over 7 is also the SportsLine model's pick.
moves: Padres opened −128 and sit −131 to −136: a small move toward San Diego.
Total is 7 at most books (over −109); one report has it opening 6.5 and moving up. About two-thirds of DraftKings money is on the Over.
Side money splits conflict between sources, and no clear sharp-money report surfaced.
